A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same 2K Retrofit work, with readable and matchable text, equations, figures, and tables. Neither contains appendix pages, despite the shared appendix reference in Section 4.1; the comparison covers all supplied material.

before.justification: v1 reports original depth-estimation and pointmap experiments, efficiency measurements, and ablations in Tables 1–5, alongside qualitative results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including benchmark comparisons, efficiency measurements, and ablations.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same frozen low-resolution backbone, entropy-based pixel selection, sparse refinement module, and gated fusion. No algorithm, architecture, training objective, or inference procedure changes.

E1.justification: The same depth and pointmap tasks use the synthetic 2K Retrofit dataset, ARKitScenes, ScanNet++, ETH3D, MVS-Synth, DL3DV, and Blend-MVS. No dataset, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Tables 1–4 and the qualitative comparisons remain unchanged. Dense3R is added only to related work, without a reported evaluation.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1–4.4 retain the same splits, zero-shot settings, metrics, training budget, backbone configurations, and latency-testing conditions. Added citations do not alter the experimental protocols.

E4.justification: The entropy/error analysis, backbone generalization examples, failure cases, and four component ablations remain unchanged in Figures 4 and 6 and Table 5. Pi3 and Depth Anything v3 were already tested in v1; v3 merely supplies citations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Statistical reporting practices remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 retain the same numerical results, and the qualitative examples and reported findings are unchanged. For example, Table 2 still reports 2K Retrofit's ETH3D depth AbsRel of 0.0192 and pointmap overall error of 0.839.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(5), including the entropy and gated-fusion definitions, are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, propositions, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about efficient 2K geometry prediction, sparse refinement, compatibility with frozen backbones, and accuracy–efficiency advantages.

C2.justification: The explanations of sparse error concentration, component behavior, and accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs remain unchanged. Both versions retain the same limitations involving reflective surfaces, transparent objects, and low-texture regions.

D1.justification: Both versions disclose the same Omniverse-generated 50K frames, 13 training epochs, batch size 8, two RTX A6000 GPUs, and RTX 4090 FP16 latency testing. The promise to release code upon acceptance is unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds bibliography entries for Dens3r, Pi3, and Depth Anything 3. Section 2.2 adds Dense3R and Pi3 to its examples, Section 4.5 cites the already-tested backbones, and Section 2.3 repairs two unresolved SparseRefine citations to an existing reference. The overall research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Author affiliations are revised, related-work wording receives a small expansion, and citation markers are added or repaired. The section order and nearly all prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The title-page affiliation block is reformatted, and added references cause local text wrapping and bibliography reflow onto another page. Figures 1–6 and Tables 1–5 retain their visual designs and placement.

improvement.justification: Repairing the unresolved SparseRefine citations and adding references for previously discussed or tested models improves attribution and traceability. Related-work coverage is slightly broader, while the method, experimental evidence, and limitations remain unchanged, making the overall benefit modest.
